text:
omar: FYI seeing a sudden metadata storm on us-central2 local-NVMe group. Lots of remap growth and write stalls, GPU attach p99 spiking. Started ~5m ago.
zoe: any specific nodes?
omar: hot nodes: gnode-701, gnode-706, gnode-719. sample kernel excerpt: 
```
[ 54321.987654] nvme1: remap growth triggered, entries 2048->16384, meta_sync=EIO
[ 54322.001234] nvme1: metadata write failure, errno=-5, retrying (attempt=3)
[ 54322.456700] block: writeback_cgroup pause, io_stall=1s
```
priya: that pattern looks like remap amplification + concurrent compaction. Did we schedule aggressive compaction for the region?
devops-bot: NOTE ops-flags: region.us-central2.kv_compaction="aggressive" was enabled 2026-04-08T02:00Z.
zoe: ugh. we also bumped scrub concurrency last week for cold-pool reclaim.
englead: immediate mitigation options: 1) reduce kv_compaction to "low" for us-central2, 2) throttle scrub concurrency to 1 regionally, 3) annotate top-10 hot nodes with `warehouse.redwood/scrub-paused=true`, 4) cordon hot nodes for new GPU attaches if needed. Prefer minimal blast radius first.
ops-coordinator: cost aside, if we spill to us-west backup, expect ~ $1.1k/day egress + accelerated preemptible churn — prefer local fixes.
omar: executing option 1+2 now. patching ops-flags and restarting compactor service (rolling).
priya: I'll annotate the three hottest nodes and add them to avoid-pool for new attaches: `kubectl annotate node gnode-701 warehouse.redwood/scrub-paused=true` and `kubectl taint nodes gnode-701 gpu.attach-block=1:NoSchedule` for gnode-701/706/719.
devops-bot: ALERT us-central2 nvme.remap_rate=920/s across 11 nodes - incident_id=INC-20260420-2201
zoe: also toggle feature-flag `scrub-on-attach=false` to reduce attach-time metadata writes. Patching now.
(90s)
omar: remap rate down ~60%, attach p99 improved from 28s -> 6.5s. partial recovery.
englead: good. let's hold these mitigations for 90m, then do a canary: remove annotations on gnode-719 and resume scrub with lower concurrency to observe.
priya: filing STORAGE-835 to track telemetry and correlate with firmware rollout (controller fw v2.14 applied 2026-04-05 to cohort A).
ops-coordinator: notifying Dedicated account owners in us-central2; flagging potential SLO impact window.
devops-bot: NOTE incident=INC-20260420-2201 has been acknowledged by oncall and assigned to storage-team.
zoe: long-term action items: add remap-growth circuit-breaker to scrub-controller, adaptive compaction backoff, and an interlock between network-recovery and scrub runs (avoid heavy metadata ops during fabric heals). I'll draft RFC and link here.
englead: also gather SMART and NVMe namespace telemetry for these nodes and run a targeted scrub-health audit. Prioritize root-cause before any firmware rollback.
(3m later)
omar: monitoring shows stability. remap_rate steady < 150/s, attach p99 ~3.2s. :white_check_mark:
priya: will keep annotations and low compaction for 90m then slowly revert via canary.
ops-coordinator: thanks team. please post postmortem notes in STORAGE-835 and RFC when ready. closing thread after 2h stable window. :eyes:
